translator: Claude (AI), draft, not reviewed by a specialist
intro: An Akkadian therapeutic text copied at Ḫattuša (CTH 808): a series of alternative recipes ('ditto') for poultices, in which long lists of plants and aromatics are crushed, mixed with flour, boiled in beer or wine into a paste and bandaged onto the patient. Scribes added Hittite, Luwian(?) and Hurrian glosses, including the candid note 'this ṣalabita I do not know'; the reverse turns to a purification rite with Hittite notes.

sections.title: Further recipe and a purification rite (fragmentary)

paras.en: […] all(?) … man(?) […] …; the ḪA.AB-plant, Ú.RA.AN.NA-plant, juniper (ŠIM.LI), […]-aromatic, [ni]nû-plant: you crush (them) (and) mix (them) together as one; you boil (them) in kasû-juice (A GAZI), and you keep bandaging (him).

Ditto: cress (ZÀ.AḪ.LI), ḫašû-plant, … [GI.K]Ù.GA-reed(?), bread of roasted grain (NINDA ŠE.SA.A), 'scorpion'-plant (GÍR.TAB), 'fox-grape' (GEŠTIN.KA₅.A), fenugreek (šanbaliltu): you crush (them); you boil (them) in first-quality beer; you decoct (it) like a rabīku-paste (Hittite gloss: 'he cooks it like a ḫuwarti-'), (and) you keep bandaging that man.

Ditto: 'aromatic of Ninurta' (ŠIM dNinurta), urnû-plant, azupīru-plant: you crush (them), you boil (them) in first-quality beer, you decoct (it) like a rabīku-paste, (and) you keep bandaging that man.

Ditto: cedar (EREN), ṣalabita-wood (gloss: 'this ṣalabita I do not know'), daprānu-wood, seed of kanaktu-wood, myrtle (assa), ŠIM.AŠ-aromatic, niqiptu-wood, 'fox-grape', [s]īḫu(?)-plant, zupuḫra-plant, būšānu-plant, [i]nzuruḫa-plant, juniper, argānu-plant, 'sweet reed' (GI.DU₁₀.GA), kukru-aromatic (ŠIM.GÚR.GÚR), ŠIM.GAM.MA-aromatic, šimeššalû-aromatic (ŠIM.ŠEM.ŠE.LÁ), kirkiriyanna-wood, burāšu (juniper), myrrh (ŠIM.ŠEŠ), sīḫu-plant, argānu-plant, seed of šunû-wood, ḫašû-plant, tamarisk (bīnu), IN.NU.UŠ-plant (maštakal), date palm, GI.ŠUL(.ḪI)-reed: all these aromatics you crush with a (wooden) crusher (GIŠGAZ) (gloss: mamanaššati battunāti puwāti, 'with pestle(?) (and) mortar(?), pounding(?)'); you mix (them) together with emmer flour; you decoct (it) in pressed wine (GEŠTIN.SUR.RA) like a rabīku-paste, (and) you keep bandaging that man.

Ditto: azupīru-plant, fenugreek (šanbaliltu), azukirānu-wood, […]-wood, (called) šattiyarḫinni in Hurrian, the […]mi-plant, karšu-wood, TIR.TIR-plant (gloss: paršunti[…]), šamutta-plant, coriander (ŠE.LÚ), ḫuršan-plant, cress, šinburatu-plant, Ú.RA.AN.NA-plant, šunû-wood: you mix (them) together; you mix (them) with emmer flour (ZÌ kunāši); you decoct (it) in pressed wine like a rabīku-paste, (and) you bandage that man.

Ditto: urpatu-plant, 'silver-fruit' plant (GURUN.KÙ.BABBAR), ninû-plant, ata'išu-plant, 'scorpion'-plant, sīḫu-plant, argānu-plant, šunû-plant, SULLIM-plant, fenugreek (šanbaliltu), UR.PÍ.PÍ-plant, ḪAŠḪUR-akî-wood and (gloss: kubbin), KI.dIŠKUR-plant, […]-plant, pakkišittu-plant (gloss: […]ammarḫuwaš), ata'išu-plant: you mix (them) together with emmer flour; you boil (them) [in] first-quality beer; you decoct (it) like a rabīku-paste, (and) you keep bandaging that man.

Ditto: seed of Ú.RA.AN.NA, [š]akirû-plant, seed of ḫurzan-plant, seed of nuḫurtu, seed of šun[û]-wood, kubbin, kalbānu-plant, zuḫata-plant, ḫašû-plant, seed of urnû(?) […], seed of TIN.KIR.GI₆-plant, seed of šinburatu-plant, pak[kišittu]-plant, …-abbul, seed of ganaṣūtu, seed of ḫuwal[li]-plant, [see]d of ala[mi]-plant (in Hurrian), cress, seed of šamīdu-plant, […]…, 'silver-fruit' plant, seed of 'gold-fruit' (GURUN.KÙ.SI₂₂), ašūḫu-plant, seed of ninû-plant, seed of pillû, seed of cress (gloss?: gimra), seed of sīḫu, seed of argānu, seed of SIKIL-plant, ḪAŠḪUR-akî-plant, seed of daprānu, seed of ni[n]û(?)-wood, kanaktu-aromatic (ŠIM.GIG), seed of šimeššalû, seed of ašūḫu-wood: you mix (them) with [ghe]e, you mix (them) in first-quality beer, and you keep bandaging him.
[…] … and he prepares (it) (Hittite: nu ḫandāizzi). [In] beer you put (it)(?) … […]

imḫur-l[imu]-plant, [ḪAŠḪUR-ak]î-plant, […]-plant [break] […] … […] the sick man … […] you perform [a puri]fication (takpirtu) … […] a ḫulduppû (substitute animal?) … […] … ḫuldupa- … […] …azzuk […] … šezzû(?), after it … […] you bind(?) the [s]ick man […] [whethe]r two months [or] three months […] you shall keep doing thus.
[Hittite:] […] … the word (memian); but beyond this (point) I know (it)(?).
[…] … purification (takpirtu), NAM.TAR.E.MAḪ-s […] [Hittite:] … they perform […], and they perform just those.
